Bottom line (MEDIUM confidence): a bottom-up buildup puts the 5 MWh molten-salt TES installed cost at roughly $400/kWh_th — 10-25× the utility-scale CSP benchmark, because tanks, heat exchangers, pumps, and instrumentation carry near-fixed minimum costs that don't shrink with a small plant's capacity. For direct heat delivery that levelizes to a reasonable 10-19¢/kWh_th. But routed through a power block to deliver electricity, a further ~3× efficiency penalty (resistive-heater → thermal-storage → small-heat-engine round trip, ~31%) pushes the cost to 41-75¢/kWh_e — roughly 3× a comparably sized Li-ion system's 13-25¢/kWh_e. Recommendation: use Li-ion for 5 MWh grid electricity storage; molten-salt TES is cost-competitive at this scale only when the delivered product is heat, not electricity.
